knowledge:
- key_parameters: geneIds=A vector of unique gene identifiers (typically Entrez Gene IDs) representing the selected list of interest (e.g., differentially expressed genes) ;; universeGeneIds=A vector of unique gene identifiers representing the background universe of genes, which should be filtered to match the assayed/expressed genes ;; annotation=A string specifying the metadata annotation package corresponding to the platform used (e.g., "hgu95av2.db") ;; ontology=A two-letter string specifying the GO ontology to test: "BP" (Biological Process), "CC" (Cellular Component), or "MF" (Molecular Function) ;; pvalueCutoff=A numeric value between 0 and 1 used as a threshold for significance and for determining which child terms are conditioned out in conditional testing ;; conditional=A logical value; if TRUE, child terms that are significant at the pvalueCutoff are conditioned out when testing parent terms to account for the DAG structure ;; testDirection=A string, either "over" or "under", specifying whether to test for over- or under-representation of categories ;; geneSetCollection=A GeneSetCollection object from the GSEABase package, used to pass custom GO or KEGG mappings for unsupported organisms
- alternatives: AnnotationForge=Used to check if an organism is supported by standard annotation packages via available.dbschemas() ;; Category=Provides KEGGHyperGParams and PFAMHyperGParams for testing KEGG pathways and PFAM domains in supported organisms ;; multtest=Used for computing adjusted p-values (e.g., mt.maxT) during the upstream gene selection stage
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have a list of genes of interest (e.g., from a differential expression analysis) and want to find significantly associated GO terms or KEGG pathways, while controlling for the hierarchical structure of GO terms (using conditional testing) and defining a custom gene universe.
- pitfalls: Pitfall 1: Using an overly broad gene universe (like the entire genome) instead of restricting it to genes actually expressed or assayed in the experiment, which artificially inflates significance (produces lower p-values) ;; Pitfall 2: Failing to map multiple probes to a single unique Entrez Gene ID, which leads to double-counting GO categories ;; Pitfall 3: Ignoring the directionality of gene expression changes (e.g., mixing up-regulated and down-regulated genes in a single list), which can mask direction-specific GO associations ;; Pitfall 4: Forgetting that genes without any GO annotations in the specified ontology are discarded during hyperGTest, which reduces the effective size of the gene list and universe

workflows.name: go_association_supported_organism
workflows.intent: Perform standard or conditional hypergeometric testing for GO term association using a standard Bioconductor annotation package.
input: expression_data.RData (An ExpressionSet object containing microarray or transcriptomics expression values)
workflows.stages: 1. Filter out probes without Entrez Gene IDs or GO annotations. 2. Apply non-specific filtering based on Inter-Quartile Range (IQR) and remove Y-chromosome genes to reduce bias. 3. Resolve probe-to-gene redundancy by keeping the probe with the largest IQR for each Entrez ID. 4. Define the gene universe and select differentially expressed genes using a t-test. 5. Construct a GOHyperGParams parameter object. 6. Run the hypergeometric test using hyperGTest. 7. Summarize results and generate an HTML report.
workflows.code:
entrezIds <- mget(featureNames(bcrAblOrNeg), envir=hgu95av2ENTREZID)
haveEntrezId <- names(entrezIds)[sapply(entrezIds, function(x) !is.na(x))]
bcrAblOrNeg <- bcrAblOrNeg[haveEntrezId, ]
haveGo <- sapply(mget(featureNames(bcrAblOrNeg), hgu95av2GO), function(x){ if (length(x) == 1 && is.na(x)) FALSE else TRUE })
bcrAblOrNeg <- bcrAblOrNeg[haveGo, ]
bcrAblOrNegIqr <- apply(exprs(bcrAblOrNeg), 1, IQR)
selected <- bcrAblOrNegIqr > iqrCutoff
chrN <- mget(featureNames(bcrAblOrNeg), envir=hgu95av2CHR)
onY <- sapply(chrN, function(x) any(x=="Y"))
onY[is.na(onY)] <- FALSE
selected <- selected & !onY
nsFiltered <- bcrAblOrNeg[selected, ]
uniqGenes <- findLargest(featureNames(nsFiltered), nsFilteredIqr, "hgu95av2")
nsFiltered <- nsFiltered[uniqGenes, ]
affyUniverse <- featureNames(nsFiltered)
entrezUniverse <- unlist(mget(affyUniverse, hgu95av2ENTREZID))
ttests = rowttests(nsFiltered, "mol.biol")
smPV = ttests$p.value < ttestCutoff
pvalFiltered <- nsFiltered[smPV, ]
selectedEntrezIds <- unlist(mget(featureNames(pvalFiltered), hgu95av2ENTREZID))
params <- new("GOHyperGParams", geneIds=selectedEntrezIds, universeGeneIds=entrezUniverse, annotation="hgu95av2.db", ontology="BP", pvalueCutoff=hgCutoff, conditional=FALSE, testDirection="over")
paramsCond <- params
conditional(paramsCond) <- TRUE
hgOver <- hyperGTest(params)
hgCondOver <- hyperGTest(paramsCond)
df <- summary(hgOver)
pvalues(hgOver)[1:3]
oddsRatios(hgOver)[1:3]
expectedCounts(hgOver)[1:3]
geneCounts(hgOver)[1:3]
universeCounts(hgOver)[1:3]
length(geneIds(hgOver))
length(geneIdUniverse(hgOver)[[3]])
goDag(hgOver)
geneMappedCount(hgOver)
universeMappedCount(hgOver)
conditional(hgOver)
testDirection(hgOver)
testName(hgOver)
htmlReport(hgCondOver, file="ALL_hgco.html")

workflows.name: association_unsupported_organism
workflows.intent: Perform GO or KEGG enrichment analysis for an organism that does not have a pre-built Bioconductor annotation package.
input: custom_go_mappings.txt (Tab-delimited file with GO ID, Evidence Code, and Gene ID)
custom_kegg_mappings.txt (Tab-delimited file with KEGG Pathway ID and Gene ID)
workflows.stages: 1. Load custom GO/KEGG mappings into a data frame. 2. Create a GOFrame or KEGGFrame object. 3. Convert GOFrame to GOAllFrame to automatically populate the parent-child graph relationships. 4. Generate a GeneSetCollection using GSEABase. 5. Define the gene list and universe. 6. Set up a GSEAGOHyperGParams or GSEAKEGGHyperGParams object. 7. Run hyperGTest and extract the summary.
workflows.code:
frame = toTable(org.Hs.egGO)
goframeData = data.frame(frame$go_id, frame$Evidence, frame$gene_id)
goFrame=GOFrame(goframeData,organism="Homo sapiens")
goAllFrame=GOAllFrame(goFrame)
gsc <- GeneSetCollection(goAllFrame, setType = GOCollection())
universe = Lkeys(org.Hs.egGO)
genes = universe[1:500]
params <- GSEAGOHyperGParams(name="My Custom GSEA based annot Params", geneSetCollection=gsc, geneIds = genes, universeGeneIds = universe, ontology = "MF", pvalueCutoff = 0.05, conditional = FALSE, testDirection = "over")
Over <- hyperGTest(params)
head(summary(Over))
frame = toTable(org.Hs.egPATH)
keggframeData = data.frame(frame$path_id, frame$gene_id)
keggFrame=KEGGFrame(keggframeData,organism="Homo sapiens")
gsc <- GeneSetCollection(keggFrame, setType = KEGGCollection())
universe = Lkeys(org.Hs.egGO)
genes = universe[1:500]
kparams <- GSEAKEGGHyperGParams(name="My Custom GSEA based annot Params", geneSetCollection=gsc, geneIds = genes, universeGeneIds = universe, pvalueCutoff = 0.05, testDirection = "over")
kOver <- hyperGTest(params)
head(summary(kOver))

workflows.name: go_visualization_and_similarity
workflows.intent: Visualize phenotype expression patterns on an induced GO graph and calculate semantic similarity distances between genes based on GO annotations.
input: expression_data.RData (An ExpressionSet object containing expression values)
selected_genes.txt (A list of Entrez Gene IDs of interest)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate mean expression per phenotype group for each gene. 2. Map GO terms to probes and classify them based on the phenotype with the highest mean. 3. Render the induced GO graph with nodes represented as pie charts. 4. Construct individual GO graphs for genes of interest. 5. Compute semantic similarity matrices using Union-Intersection (simUI) and Longest Path (simLP) methods. 6. Identify leaf nodes of the GO graph.
workflows.code:
mns <- apply(exprs(eS), 1, function(x) sapply(split(x, MB), mean))
whismax <- apply(mns, 2, function(x) match(max(x), x))
maxNames <- names(mns[, 1])[whismax]
names(maxNames) <- names(whismax)
CCnodes <- nodes(gCC)
nodes2affy <- mget(CCnodes, hgu95av2GO2ALLPROBES, ifnotfound = NA)
cts <- sapply(nodes2affy, function(x) { wh <- names(whismax) %in% x; table(maxNames[wh]) })
all1cts <- sapply(cts, function(x) x["ALL1/AF4"])
all1cts <- ifelse(is.na(all1cts), 0, all1cts)
names(all1cts) <- names(cts)
bcrcts <- sapply(cts, function(x) x["BCR/ABL"])
bcrcts <- ifelse(is.na(bcrcts), 0, bcrcts)
names(bcrcts) <- names(cts)
negcts <- sapply(cts, function(x) x["NEG"])
negcts <- ifelse(is.na(negcts), 0, negcts)
names(negcts) <- names(cts)
ctmat <- cbind(all1cts, bcrcts, negcts)
plotPieChart(gCClo, ctmat)
igenes <- unlist(mget(gN[1:10], hgu95av2ENTREZID))
igenes <- igenes[!is.na(igenes)]
igenes <- as.character(igenes)
psets <- mget(igenes, revmap(hgu95av2ENTREZID))
psets <- sapply(psets, function(x) x[1])
GOs <- mget(psets, hgu95av2GO, ifnotfound = NA)
gBP <- sapply(GOs, getOntology, "BP")
hasBP <- sapply(gBP, function(x) length(x) > 0 && !is.na(x[1]))
gBP <- gBP[hasBP]
ggs <- lapply(igenes[hasBP], makeGOGraph, "BP", chip = "hgu95av2.db")
simatM1 <- matrix(1, nr = sum(hasBP), nc = sum(hasBP))
for (i in 1:sum(hasBP)) { for (j in 1:sum(hasBP)) { if (i == j) { next } else { simatM1[i, j] <- simUI(ggs[[i]], ggs[[j]]) } } }
simatM2 <- matrix(1, nr = sum(hasBP), nc = sum(hasBP))
for (i in 1:sum(hasBP)) { for (j in 1:sum(hasBP)) { if (i == j) { next } else { simatM2[i, j] <- simLP(ggs[[i]], ggs[[j]]) } } }
gCC.leaves <- leaves(gCC, "in")
